entities.name: FtsH ATP-dependent protease
observations: 652 aa bacterial membrane-anchored ATP-dependent zinc metalloprotease candidate.
Sequence-derived mass is 71.5 kDa; theoretical pI 5.81; predicted charge at pH 7 is −6.8.
Contains two N-terminal hydrophobic transmembrane helices, approximately residues 19–39 and 116–136, separated by a periplasmic loop; the large C-terminal domain is cytoplasmic.
Pfam domains: FtsH_ext residues 21–110, AAA residues 206–338, AAA_lid_3 residues 360–403, and Peptidase_M41 residues 419–607.
Shares 60.9–62.3% identity and 92.8–95.4% query coverage with reviewed FtsH proteins Q1LLA9, P63344, and P63343.
Likely forms a homohexamer and functions in ATP-dependent degradation of cytoplasmic and integral membrane proteins; these functional and oligomeric assignments are homology-based.
Expected cofactor is one catalytic Zn2+ per subunit in the M41 protease domain; no explicit reaction equation was retrieved.
Predicted activities include ATP binding/hydrolysis, ATP-dependent proteolysis, zinc-dependent metalloendopeptidase activity, and membrane protein quality control.

source_tools.relevance: Sequence properties, Pfam domains, homology, localization, function, cofactor, subunit, and GO evidence

entities.name: Q1LLA9
observations: Reviewed Cupriavidus metallidurans FtsH reference protein; 62.3% identity to the query over 92.8% query coverage.
Annotated as an ATP-dependent zinc metalloprotease localized to the cell inner membrane, with homohexameric subunit organization.

entities.name: P63344
observations: Reviewed Salmonella typhi FtsH reference protein; 60.9% identity to the query over 95.4% query coverage.
Annotated for ATP-dependent zinc metalloprotease activity, inner-membrane localization, zinc binding, and homohexamer formation.

entities.name: Membrane protein quality control
observations: FtsH homologs participate in proteolytic quality control of integral membrane proteins and can also degrade cytoplasmic substrates.

source_tools.relevance: Curated functional annotation of close FtsH homologs

entities.name: FtsH zinc-dependent proteolysis
observations: The M41 peptidase domain and close reviewed homologs support Zn2+-dependent ATP-coupled proteolysis; the exact reaction equation was not retrieved.

source_tools.relevance: Pfam Peptidase_M41 domain and reviewed FtsH annotations
